4.1 INTRODUCTION TO FAULT DETECTION
One of the most important tasks in the elucidation of reservoir structure is the 
identification of any linear sealing faults of the type illustrated diagrammatically in 
Figure 1.  This is of particular concern where recovery by displacement is envisaged 
and knowledge of the continuity between wells is essential.  The first evidence 
of the existence of faulting is usually obtained when recognisable zones show a 
displacement in depth between two wells after allowing for formation inclination; 
obviously the dip-meter is the key log in this exercise.  Single well testing may be 
able to confirm the presence of a linear boundary. However, in order to determine 
whether a fault is completely sealing or exhibits partial communication, it may be 
necessary to carry out interference tests.  The effect of a linear no-flow boundary
